stories.head: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
stories.fact: Anthropic released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, describing coding, reasoning and vision improvements. They share an underlying model; Fable has safeguards supporting broad access, while Mythos access uses verification programs.
stories.why: Benchmark MATLAB code generation against fixed correctness tests, latency and cost before changing the production model.
stories.unc: Performance claims are vendor evaluations, not independent evidence of reliable financial decisions.
stories.alt: Conceptual labels show one underlying model, broad Fable access, verified Mythos access and a local MATLAB benchmark gate.

stories.head: Boolean factor screens expose interaction trading costs
stories.fact: Wang, Rachev and Fabozzi decompose Boolean portfolio rules into individual signals and interactions. Their U.S. stock study links higher-order interactions to lower persistence and higher turnover, and compares threshold rules with smoother products of ranks.
stories.why: Compare hard screening intersections with smooth rank weights at matched risk, including spread and market-impact costs.
stories.unc: This is a preprint with author backtests. Quoted-spread estimates do not capture every execution cost or establish future alpha.
labels: Test smooth ranks at matched risk
stories.alt: Conceptual labels connect Boolean rules to signal interactions, turnover, rank information loss and a matched-risk comparison.

stories.head: Nasdaq futures lag the Dow before CPI
stories.fact: At 6:04 a.m. EST, Reuters reported Dow futures up 0.30%, S&P 500 futures up 0.01%, and Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.35%.
stories.why: Monitor ES/NQ relative strength and SPY/QQQ execution conditions separately; a positive broad-market headline can hide growth weakness.
stories.unc: Earlier reported snapshot, not live executable prices. These changes reveal neither spreads nor order-book depth.
stories.alt: Three labels show Dow and S&P futures higher and Nasdaq futures lower at the same November 10 checkpoint.

stories.head: October CPI is due at 7:30 a.m. CST today
stories.fact: The BLS calendar schedules October 2026 Consumer Price Index data for Tuesday November 10 at 8:30 a.m. EST, equivalent to 7:30 a.m. CST / 13:30 UTC. Results were unavailable at the research cutoff.
stories.why: Stress event gaps and spread expansion; compare actual headline and core readings with a timestamped consensus only after release.
stories.unc: This is release scheduling, not an inflation forecast. No CPI outcome or immediate market reaction is asserted.
stories.credit: Bureau of Labor Statistics, November 2026 calendar
stories.alt: Calendar labels show the October reference month and November 10 CPI release at 7:30 CST, with the outcome marked unknown.

stories.head: CoreWeave signs multiyear Wayve cloud agreement
stories.fact: CoreWeave announced a multiyear agreement to support Wayve’s AI-driver development with its cloud and NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, covering training, evaluation and simulation.
stories.why: Track capacity utilization, customer diversification and cash requirements; distinguish contracted demand from recognized revenue.
stories.unc: Financial terms and the agreement’s revenue contribution were not disclosed. A capacity agreement alone does not establish profitability.
stories.alt: Labels connect Wayve AI-driver development to training, evaluation and simulation on CoreWeave Blackwell infrastructure, with terms undisclosed.
